metadata.case_name: LAU CHUNG NAM v. AU WAI MAN

plaintiff.expected_occupation_after: sheltered workshop for one year then simple non-intellectually demanding work (e.g. cleaner, gas station attendant, clerk, cashier, messenger or receptionist)

injuries.description: severe head injury with radiological investigation revealing a right intercerebral haemorrhage and a left frontal epidural haematoma as well as a right frontal cerebral contusion; right frontal lobectomy performed
source: He was found to have sustained a severe head injury with radiological investigation revealing a right intercerebral haemorrhage and a left frontal epidural haematoma as well as a right frontal cerebral contusion.
Emergency operation for evacuation of epidural haematoma ... was performed on the plaintiff the same day.
a further operation for right frontal lobectomy was performed the next day.

injuries.description: post-traumatic epilepsy with regular epileptic seizures and convulsions
source: Since that time, he has had regular epileptic seizures and convulsions, very often resulting in the dislocation of his left shoulder.
The epileptic attacks to the plaintiff had improved since he began consulting Dr Jason Fong in December 2002.
injuries.icd_description: Epilepsy due to injuries to the head

injuries.description: moderate cognitive impairment / cognitive deficits resulting from head injury
source: Full cognitive assessment in mid-June showed mildly impaired intelligence, mildly impaired attention and visual memory.

Dr Lau further states that although orthopaedically there should be nothing preventing the plaintiff from returning to his pre-accident work as a cook, in fact he cannot do so because of the permanent cognitive impairment resulting from the head injury.
Professor Lee ... concluded ... he still has unresolved post-traumatic epilepsy and a moderate degree of cognitive impairment.

injuries.description: fracture to the spinal process at C3 (fractured cervical spine at the C3 spinal process)
source: He also suffered a fractured cervical spine at the C3 spinal process.
The fracture to his spinal process at C3 was treated conservatively.
Dr Lau was also of the view that the fracture to the spinal process at C3 has completely recovered.
injuries.icd_description: Fracture of other specified cervical vertebra

injuries.description: comminuted fracture of left tibia and fibula
source: There was a comminuted fracture of his left tibia and fibula.
Emergency operation for ... closed reduction and external fixation of the fractured left tibia and fibula was performed on the plaintiff the same day.

Dr Lau Hoi Kuen whose report dated 24 November 2001 stated that the plaintiff had made an excellent recovery from his fracture to the left tibia and fibula and that the range of movement of his left knee and ankle joint is well preserved.

injuries.description: recurrent dislocation / instability of left shoulder (often resulting from epileptic convulsions)
source: Since that time, he has had regular epileptic seizures and convulsions, very often resulting in the dislocation of his left shoulder.
Although he found the shoulder to be normal when he examined the plaintiff, he commented that it could become unstable with recurrent dislocation if the epilepsy remains uncontrolled.

manifestations.description: unconscious when he first arrived at Tuen Mun Hospital
post-traumatic amnesic phase; disorientated and non-communicative showing non-purposeful movements of limbs
motor power of the left limbs reduced to grade three out of five

source: Emergency operation for evacuation of epidural haematoma and for closed reduction and external fixation of the fractured left tibia and fibula was performed on the plaintiff the same day.

treatments_received.treatment: closed reduction and external fixation of the fractured left tibia and fibula
source: Emergency operation for evacuation of epidural haematoma and for closed reduction and external fixation of the fractured left tibia and fibula was performed on the plaintiff the same day.
treatments_received.vmis_procedure: Closed reduction for fracture of upper arm / lower arm / wrist / hand / leg / foot bone without internal fixation

source: a further operation for right frontal lobectomy was performed the next day.
Post operatively, the plaintiff was transferred to the Intensive Care Unit where he stayed until 19 April 2000.

treatments_received.treatment: bone grafting and adjustment of external fixation
source: Bone grafting and adjustment of external fixation was performed on him on 4 July 2000.
treatments_received.vmis_procedure: Operative treatment of compound fracture with external fixator and extensive wound debridement

treatments_received.treatment: removal of external fixator from lower left leg
source: The plaintiff was re-admitted to the orthopaedic department of Tuen Mun Hospital on 18 August 2000 for removal of the external fixator from his lower left leg.
treatments_received.vmis_procedure: Removal of screw, pin and plate, and other metal for old fracture except fracture femur

treatments_received.treatment: conservative treatment for fracture to spinal process at C3
source: The fracture to his spinal process at C3 was treated conservatively.

treatments_received.treatment: rehabilitation (transfer to Kowloon Hospital for rehabilitation)
source: The plaintiff was transferred to Kowloon Hospital for rehabilitation on 27 April 2000.

treatments_future.treatment: trial of newer antiepileptic drugs and ongoing management of epilepsy
source: Dr Choa is somewhat critical of the hospital treating the plaintiff for his epilepsy in that since its onset, the plaintiff has been on a single antiepileptic drug. It seems that no steps had been taken to try out newer antiepileptic drugs in the case of the plaintiff albeit that the newer drugs are more expensive but are able to control otherwise uncontrollable epilepsy.

treatments_future.treatment: epilepsy surgery (suggested as a possibility if drugs fail)
source: If these newer drugs fail, Dr Choa suggests epilepsy surgery as another possibility.

treatments_future.treatment: regular follow up for management of his epilepsy
source: Dr Woo says that the plaintiff needs regular follow up for management of his epilepsy but that there is no reason for the plaintiff's epilepsy care to be transferred to the private sector.

losses.description: Because of his epilepsy the plaintiff is not allowed to go out on his own thus his repertoire of social and leisure activities have narrowed significantly and he has not been in contact with his previous friends.

Although orthopaedically able to return to his pre-accident work as a cook, he cannot do so because of the permanent cognitive impairment resulting from the head injury; difficulty coping with open employment.

losses.category: Loss of confidence in going out in the public
losses.description: Because of his epilepsy the plaintiff is not allowed to go out on his own.
